domains.title: Ātma Pratibimba
domains.subtitle: Who Am I? And What Is This World?
domains.summary: The world reflects consciousness, and liberation comes through realizing the Self alone is real.
domains.description:
The world appears vast and separate, yet it is known only because consciousness illumines it. Just as a city reflected in a mirror has no existence apart from the mirror, the universe is experienced only within the light of awareness. In the same way that a dream seems real until we awaken, the waking world appears upon the screen of consciousness.

The feeling of separation between "I" and "the world" arises because of Māyā, the power that makes the One appear as many. When this ignorance is removed through the grace of Sri Dakshinamurthy, one discovers that the witness of every experience is none other than one's own limitless Self—unchanging, ever-present, and of the nature of bliss.
domains.quote: Viśvaṁ darpaṇa-dṛśyamāna-nagarī-tulyaṁ nijāntargataṁ paśyannātmani māyayā bahirivodbhūtaṁ yathā nidrayā; yaḥ sākṣāt kurute prabodha-samaye svātmānam evādvayaṁ tasmai śrī-gurumūrtaye nama idaṁ śrī-dakṣiṇāmūrtaye.
practiceSteps: Find a comfortable posture, spine aligned like a lightning rod of energy.
Inhale golden cosmic prana for 4 seconds, feeling it rise from your root.
Hold the light at your crown chakra for 4 seconds, visualizing a lotus expanding.
Exhale slowly for 4 seconds, releasing temporal anxieties into primeval space.
Hold your lungs empty for 4 seconds, resting in pure unmanifested consciousness.

domains.title: JAGAD BĪJĀṄKURA
domains.subtitle: Like a Sprout Within a Seed, the Universe Unfolds
domains.summary: The universe unfolds from blissful consciousness and appears diverse through māyā.
domains.description:
The entire universe emerges from Iswara, whose true nature is pure consciousness and bliss. Before creation, the world existed in an unmanifest state, just as a great tree exists in potential within a tiny seed. Through the power of Māyā, this hidden potential unfolds into the countless names and forms that make up the universe.

Just as a magician creates appearances without changing reality, Iswara appears as the world while remaining the one unchanging truth. Understanding this reveals that creation is not separate from the Divine—it is the Divine expressing itself through infinite forms.
domains.quote: Bījasya-antar-ivāṅkuro jagad-idaṁ prāṅ-nirvikalpaṁ punaḥ māyā-kalpita-deśa-kāla-kalanā-vaicitrya-citrī-kṛtam | māyāvīva vijṛmbhayaty-api mahā-yogīva yaḥ svecchayā tasmai śrī-gurumūrtaye nama idaṁ śrī-dakṣiṇāmūrtaye ||
practiceSteps: Visualize a tiny, silent seed resting in the dark soil of pure consciousness, containing the potential of a massive, ancient tree.
Observe how the sprout of the universe emerges, expanding into space, time, and varied forms through the power of illusion (Māyā).
Recognize that the diverse world is but a projection of your own inner reality, like a magic show created by a master magician.
Rest in the blissful, undifferentiated state of 'Nirvikalpa' prior to names and forms, identifying with the source rather than the projection.

domains.title: SPHURAṆA JYOTI
domains.subtitle: The Light Behind Every Experience
domains.summary: Liberation arises by realizing the Self and bliss are one.
domains.description:
The Self alone is eternal and unchanging. The world appears from it just as waves arise from the ocean—different in appearance, yet never separate from the water itself. Every form, every object, and every experience is sustained by the same underlying consciousness.

Through the guidance of the Guru, one realizes that the bliss being sought has always been one's own true nature. When this truth is understood, the illusion of separation fades, and the world is seen as an expression of the same limitless Self.
domains.quote: yasyaiva sphuraṇaṁ sadātmakam asat-kalpārthakaṁ bhāsate sākṣāt tat tvam asīti veda-vacasā yo bodhayaty āśritān | yat-sākṣāt-karaṇād bhaven na punar āvṛttir bhavāmbhonidhau tasmai śrī-gurumūrtaye nama idaṁ śrī-dakṣiṇāmūrtaye ||
practiceSteps: Reflect on the core insight: Consciousness is the light through which all experiences become known. Without awareness, no thought, sensation, or perception could ever arise.
Contemplate the Mahāvākya 'Tat Tvam Asi' (Thou Art That). The light you seek outside is the very awareness by which you seek. The observer and the ultimate reality are not separate.

Investigate the scientific question: Science explains how light enters the eyes and the brain processes information, yet what is it that knows these perceptions? Explore consciousness as the illuminating principle behind all experience.

Consider the project connection: Just as projected realities in holography and visual illusions depend on a hidden light source, all experiences depend on consciousness, which silently illuminates them.
Rest with the reflection question: Can any experience be known without awareness? Before every thought, perception, or emotion, what is the light that makes it known?

domains.title: ANTAR JYOTI
domains.subtitle: Discovering the Silent Power Within
domains.summary: Consciousness, like light inside a pot, is the hidden force within the body that enables all perception and action.
domains.description:
Imagine a lamp placed inside a pot with many small openings. Though the lamp itself cannot be seen, the light shining through the holes reveals its presence. In the same way, consciousness remains unseen, yet it is through this inner light that every thought, perception, and experience becomes possible.

The body and senses are only instruments. They cannot see, hear, or think on their own. It is the light of consciousness—the presence of Iswara within—that brings them to life. Every experience begins with the simple recognition, "I know," revealing the silent witness that shines equally in all beings.
domains.quote: The senses shine because consciousness shines.
practiceSteps: Observe the activity of the senses as they engage with the external world.
Reflect upon the silent awareness that illumines every perception and thought.
Rest in the recognition that this inner consciousness is Dakshinamurty within.

domains.title: MĀYĀ ŚAKTI VILĀSA
domains.subtitle: Why the Mind, the Breath, and the Void are Not You
domains.summary: Suffering arises from falsely identifying the Self with the body and mind, and true knowledge destroys this ignorance.
domains.description:
We often identify ourselves with the body, the senses, the mind, or our emotions, saying, "I am happy," "I am weak," or "I am this body." According to Vedanta, these are temporary conditions that belong to the body and mind, not to the true Self.

This mistaken identity arises through Māyā, just as a clear crystal appears red when placed beside a red flower. The crystal never changes; only the appearance does. Likewise, the Self remains pure, changeless, and ever-blissful, while the qualities of the body and mind are merely superimposed upon it. Recognizing this frees us from false identification and reveals our true nature.
domains.quote: Dehaṁ prāṇamapīndriyāṇyapi calāṁ buddhiṁ ca śūnyaṁ viduḥ, strībālandhajaḍopamāstvahami-ti bhrāntā bhṛśaṁ vādinaḥ; Māyāśaktivilāsakalpitamahāvyāmohasaṁhāriṇe, tasmai śrīgurumūrtaye nama idaṁ śrīdakṣiṇāmūrtaye.
practiceSteps: Observe a physical sensation or emotional wave as it rises, treating it completely like an external notification on a device.
Silently isolate the witness: strip away the labels 'I am in pain' or 'I am sad' and reframe it as 'The biological vehicle is experiencing this trajectory'.
Retract your identity fully from the sensor feedback loop of the mind-body complex, anchoring back into the unchanging observer.

domains.title: MĀYĀ ĀVARAṆA VILĀSA
domains.subtitle: The Mystery of Deep Sleep and Awareness
domains.summary: Deep sleep reveals the blissful Self hidden behind ignorance.
domains.description:
In deep sleep, the mind and senses become inactive, yet the Self continues to shine. Although we later say, "I knew nothing," this is only because ignorance veiled the experience, much like the shadow during an eclipse hides the brilliance of the sun or moon.

The very statement, "I slept peacefully," reveals that the Self was present throughout deep sleep. If there had been only emptiness, such a recollection would never be possible. Deep sleep quietly points to our true nature—a state untouched by thought, free from division, and naturally blissful.
domains.quote: Rāhugrasta divākarendu sadṛśo māyā samācchādanāt sanmātraḥ karaṇopasaṃharaṇato yo'bhūtsuṣuptaḥ pumān | prāgasvāpsamiti prabodhasamaye yaḥ pratyabhijñāyate tasmai śrī gurumūrtaye nama idaṃ śrī dakṣiṇāmūrtaye
practiceSteps: Before sleep, contemplate: What remains when the mind falls silent?
Upon waking, reflect on the thought 'I slept well' and investigate who recognized that experience.
Observe awareness as the constant presence that remains through waking, dream, and deep sleep.

domains.title: SVĀTMĀ PRAKAṬĪKARAṆA
domains.subtitle: The Self-Revealing Nature of Consciousness
domains.summary: The unchanging Self remains present through all states of experience.
domains.description:
From childhood to old age, our body changes. Our thoughts, emotions, and experiences also come and go. We pass through waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, yet throughout every change there remains one constant presence—the simple awareness we call "I."

This unchanging witness is the true Self. It does not grow older, become happier, or become weaker; it simply observes every experience. Sri Dakshinamurthy reveals this eternal witness as our own real nature, the silent presence behind every stage of life.
domains.quote:
bālyādiṣvapi jāgradādiṣu tathā sarvāsvavasthāsvapi
vyāvṛttā svanu vartamāna mahamityantaḥ sphurantaṃ sadā ।
svātmānaṃ prakaṭīkarōti bhajatāṃ yō mudrayā bhadrayā
tasmai śrī gurumūrtayē nama idaṃ śrī dakṣiṇāmūrtayē ॥ 7 ॥
practiceSteps: Observe that your consciousness is self-established and self-revealing; your existence is self-evident and not a product of logical thinking.
Investigate the changeless witness that knows your mind now and when you were a child, recognizing that the observing Consciousness remains exactly the same.
Contemplate the Chinmudra (the auspicious hand gesture) as the silent reveal of your non-separateness from the absolute Reality.

domains.title: KĀRYAKĀRAṆA SAMBANDHA
domains.subtitle: The Illusion of Cause, Effect, and Relational Diversity
domains.summary: Through māyā, the one Self appears as many forms and relations.
domains.description:
The world is filled with countless relationships—teacher and student, parent and child, master and servant. Though they appear different, they all arise within the same consciousness. It is Māyā that creates the appearance of diversity while the underlying reality remains one.

Just as a clay pot is nothing but clay given a name and form, every object in the universe is only consciousness appearing in different ways. When true knowledge arises, the many are recognized as expressions of the One, and the illusion of separation naturally dissolves.
domains.quote: Viśvaṁ paśyati kāryakāraṇatayā svasvāmisambandhataḥ śiṣyācāryatayā tathaiva pitṛputrādyātmanā bhedataḥ | svapne jāgṛti vā ya eṣa puruṣo māyāparibhrāmitaḥ tasmai śrīgurumūrtaye nama idaṁ śrīdakṣiṇāmūrtaye ||
practiceSteps: Observe the relationships in your life—parent, child, teacher, student—and see how one entity takes on multiple reciprocal roles depending on context.
Contemplate the nature of cause and effect: trace any physical object back to its cause, and notice that the cause and effect are ultimately the same substance (like clay and pot).
Reflect on the waking and dreaming states, recognizing that the one who experiences both states remains the same, untouched by the shifting states of consciousness.

domains.title: BHŪTA BRAHMĀṆḌA AIKYA
domains.subtitle: The Body as a Reflection of the Cosmos
domains.summary: Meditation reveals the body, cosmos, and consciousness as one.
domains.description:
Sri Dakshinamurthy teaches that the entire universe can be understood through eight manifestations of Iswara—earth, water, fire, air, space, the sun, the moon, and all living beings. Everything we experience belongs to one or more of these forms.

Meditating on these forms helps us recognize that the Divine is never distant. The same elements that make up the cosmos also make up our own body. By seeing Iswara in the world around us and within ourselves, everyday life becomes an opportunity for contemplation and the realization of oneness.
domains.quote: Bhūrambhāṁsyanalo'nilo'mbaramaharnātho himāṁśuḥ pumān, ityābhāti carācarātmakam idaṁ yasyaiva mūrtyaṣṭakam; nānyat kiñcana vidyate vimṛśatāṁ yasmāt parasmād vibhoḥ, tasmai śrīgurumūrtaye nama idaṁ śrīdakṣiṇāmūrtaye.
practiceSteps: Identify a negative or polarizing thought currently disturbing your mental axis.
Find its exact positive polarization (e.g., Fear to Courage, Anger to Compassion).
Focus exclusively on the highest pole, letting the lower one dissolve naturally.

domains.title: SARVĀTMATVA SPHUṬĪKARAṆA
domains.subtitle: The State of Being the Self of All
domains.summary: Realizing all as the Self brings liberation and inherent powers.
domains.description:
The Dakshinamurthy Ashtakam is more than a hymn—it is a guide to recognizing the Self. Through listening, reflection, meditation, or even sincere chanting, one gradually discovers the truth that the entire universe is none other than one's own Self.

As this understanding deepens, inner freedom naturally follows. Just as light and warmth accompany a burning flame, spiritual wisdom also brings peace, clarity, and the strength to live with greater purpose. While worldly blessings may arise along the way, the highest fruit of this practice is the realization of one's own limitless nature.
domains.quote:
sarvātmatvamiti sphuṭīkṛtamidaṃ yasmādamuṣmin stavē
tēnāsva śravaṇāttadartha mananāddhyānāchcha saṅkīrtanāt ।
sarvātmatva mahāvibhūtisahitaṃ syādīśvaratvaṃ svataḥ
siddhyēttatpunaraṣṭdhā pariṇataṃ chaiśvarya-mavyāhatam ॥ 10 ॥
practiceSteps: Reflect on the 'divine bait-and-switch': recognize that while worldly powers (Aishwarya) attract the mind, absolute happiness lies only in realizing your non-separateness from the whole.

Practice the four-fold path of absorption: listen to the sacred teachings (Shravaṇa), logically contemplate their truth (Manana), meditate on the silent witness (Dhyāna), and express/recite the non-dual reality (Saṅkīrtana).
Rest in the realization of Sarvātmatvam—the state of being the Self of all—where the boundary between the observer and the observed is completely dissolved.

articles.title: The Primordial Guru
articles.subtitle: Why do ancient sages sit before a youthful teacher?
articles.content: Beneath the shade of an ancient banyan tree sits a youthful teacher surrounded by seekers far older than himself. This is Sri Dakshinamurthy, the timeless form of Shiva as the supreme guru. Unlike ordinary teachers, he does not rely on lengthy discourses or debate. Facing the South, a direction traditionally associated with time, change, and mortality, he reveals knowledge through profound silence. For centuries, this image has inspired seekers to look beyond words and discover wisdom through direct understanding.
articles.translation: The entire universe is like a city reflected in a mirror, appearing within oneself.

articles.title: What is Daakshinaasya Darshini?
articles.subtitle: Enlightenment via Scientific Thought
articles.content:
Daakshinaasya Darshini is a science and technology exhibition inspired by Sri Dakshinamurthy, the timeless embodiment of knowledge, wisdom, and learning. Celebrating humanity's enduring quest to understand the universe, the exhibition brings together science, innovation, mathematics, and engineering under a common theme of discovery.

Through interactive exhibits, working models, and immersive visual experiences, visitors are encouraged to explore the principles that shape our world. More than a showcase of scientific ideas, Daakshinaasya Darshini invites participants to look beyond facts, ask meaningful questions, and cultivate a deeper appreciation for inquiry and understanding.

Rooted in the spirit of exploration that Dakshinamurthy symbolizes, the exhibition serves as a bridge between ancient wisdom and modern knowledge, inspiring minds to seek, discover, and learn.

It is a journey from curiosity to discovery, from discovery to understanding, and from understanding to wisdom.

articles.title: The 3-Day Exhibition
articles.subtitle: Curiosity to Discovery
articles.content:
The 3-Day Exhibition was a unique celebration of science, technology, innovation, and the timeless wisdom embodied by Sri Dakshinamurthy. Bringing together 80+ schools, 43+ outstanding projects, and 30,000+ visitors, the event created a vibrant platform for exploration, learning, and discovery.

Through interactive exhibits, working models, multimedia experiences, and engaging demonstrations, visitors explored the fascinating intersection of scientific inquiry, creativity, and human understanding.

Inspired by the vision of connecting ancient wisdom with modern knowledge, the exhibition encouraged participants to think critically, ask meaningful questions, and experience learning beyond textbooks.

More than an exhibition, it was a journey that transformed curiosity into discovery, discovery into understanding, and understanding into wisdom.

articles.title: Why are we doing this?
articles.subtitle: Discover how awareness transforms information into wisdom
articles.content:
In a world overflowing with information, knowledge alone is no longer enough. How we perceive, interpret, and respond to our experiences often shapes our understanding more than the experiences themselves. The same situation can inspire, challenge, or divide people depending on the perspective they bring to it.

Dakshinaasya Darshini was created to explore this fascinating relationship between knowledge, perception, and awareness. Through immersive exhibits, interactive experiences, and thought-provoking demonstrations, visitors are invited to examine not only the world around them but also the way they engage with it.

Inspired by the timeless teachings of Sri Dakshinamurthy, the exhibition encourages curiosity, critical thinking, and self-reflection—transforming learning into a journey from discovery to understanding, and from understanding to wisdom.

articles.title: What's Next?
articles.subtitle: The journey continues—explore the upcoming Makeathon edition
articles.content:
The journey continues. Building on the success of our exhibitions and immersive learning experiences, we are preparing the next edition of our Makeathon—an exciting platform where curiosity, creativity, and innovation come together. Staying true to the spirit of Dakshinaasya Darshini, the upcoming event will continue to explore the intersection of science, technology, and deeper understanding through engaging challenges, collaborative problem-solving, and hands-on experiences.

As plans evolve, new milestones, announcements, and event updates will be shared through the Timeline section of this website. We invite students, educators, innovators, and curious minds to follow the journey and be part of what comes next.

timeline.title: THEME ANNOUNCEMENT
timeline.subtitle: The challenge statement and categories are announced
timeline.description: Every edition begins with a clear theme that inspires innovation, problem-solving, and collaboration. The official challenge statement and competition categories are shared here to guide the journey ahead.

timeline.title: REGISTRATIONS
timeline.subtitle: Teams and individuals begin signing up
timeline.description: Registrations are open from 20 August to 20 September for interested students. Team size, eligibility criteria, registration process, and participation guidelines are available on the registration portal. Whether participating individually or as a team, this marks the beginning of your innovation journey.

timeline.title: IDEATHON
timeline.subtitle: Ideas are shortlisted for the next stage
timeline.description: If participation exceeds capacity, an ideathon will be conducted as a preliminary selection round. Teams will present their concepts before mentors and judges for the next stage.

timeline.title: EXPERT WORKSHOPS
timeline.subtitle: Guidance from mentors and industry experts
timeline.description: Qualified participants will attend expert-led workshops that build the skills, tools, and practical know-how needed to develop solutions for the final challenge.
timeline.quoteAuthor: First Week of October • Dates to be Confirmed

timeline.title: MAKEATHON FINALS
timeline.subtitle: Final prototypes and presentations
timeline.description: Shortlisted teams will transform their ideas into working prototypes, collaborate with mentors, and present their solutions before the judging panel in the final event.
